sentences.zh: 社会上依然有很大一部分人将经历精神疾病的人视为软弱、无能或无法在社会中正常运转。

sentences.zh: 药物是如何对这种污名化叙事起到推波助澜作用的，以及为什么这是一个如此重要的话题。

sentences.en: More so it's just a discussion and maybe just kind of an informational podcast on what it was like for me and what it continues to be like for me, how it impacts my life
sentences.zh: 它更多只是一场讨论，或许只是一档科普性质的播客，讲述这对我而言是怎样的经历，这种经历如何延续，它如何影响我的生活，

sentences.en: and how it has improved my life
sentences.zh: 以及它如何给我的生活带来

sentences.en: immensely.
sentences.zh: 巨大的改善。

sentences.zh: 所以，我们来聊聊20多岁时服用的抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: I think I've said this on many podcasts where I've talked about mental ill health and mental illness in the past, but you're most likely to develop signs
sentences.zh: 我想我在过去探讨心理健康受损和精神疾病的许多播客中都说过这一点，你最有可能在十几岁晚期和20岁出头时表现出

sentences.en: of any future mental ill health in your late teens and your early 20s.
sentences.zh: 未来任何心理健康问题的迹象。

sentences.en: So that's why I think it's super important to talk about where medication kind of falls into that journey whilst we are in this, in these like kind of early decades of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为在我们处于人生这前几十年的这个阶段时，探讨药物在这一历程中扮演什么角色超级重要。

sentences.en: Just so we kind of set the narrative straight around what it's really like.
sentences.zh: 好让我们理清关于真实情况的叙事。

sentences.en: So most people who experience depression or anxiety will go on some form of medication probably in this decade, probably before the age of 30, in their early 20s,
sentences.zh: 因此，大多数经历抑郁或焦虑的人，大概都会在这十年里、大概在30岁之前、在20岁出头时服用某种药物，

sentences.en: some people even in their late teens,
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至在十几岁晚期就开始了，

sentences.en: which is a little bit controversial, but it happens nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 虽然这有点争议，但它确实在发生。

sentences.en: So having a good grasp of what that actually means for your brain, what you can expect, is something that I have been pondering for a while and thought was really important
sentences.zh: 因此，对这对你的大脑究竟意味着什么有一个良好的掌握，以及了解你可以期待什么，是我一直在思考并认为非常重要的事情，

sentences.en: to talk about them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要来谈谈它们。

sentences.en: And like I've said, stigma around it is still so prevalent.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，围绕它的污名化依然非常普遍。

sentences.en: I don't need to explain that to people.
sentences.zh: 我不需要向大家解释这一点。

sentences.en: I think we see it everywhere, all the time.
sentences.zh: 我想我们随处可见，无时无刻不在看到。

sentences.en: People thinking that those with mental illness are somehow unable to hold jobs, unable to take care of their families, unable to function.
sentences.zh: 人们认为患有精神疾病的人在某种程度上无法维持工作，无法照顾家庭，无法正常生活。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that's the case, especially when medication is something that you take and something that is part of your kind of mental health journey.
sentences.zh: 但我认为事实并非如此，尤其是当你把服药作为一种治疗手段，并将其视为你的心理健康之旅的一部分时。

sentences.en: Additionally, I did some searching.
sentences.zh: 另外，我查了一下资料。

sentences.en: One in seven adult Australians are on some form of antidepressant.
sentences.zh: 七分之一的成年澳大利亚人正在服用某种抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: It is one of the 10 most prescribed drugs in Australia.
sentences.zh: 它是澳大利亚处方量前10位的药物之一。

sentences.en: So whatever stigma there may be, whatever stigma that you may hold,
sentences.zh: 所以，无论存在什么样的污名化，无论你内心可能抱有什么样的污名化，

sentences.en: I would just ask you to challenge that a little bit and think about the fact that there is probably someone in your life who has been on this medication,
sentences.zh: 我只想请你稍微挑战一下这种观念，想想这样一个事实：你的生活中可能就有人正在服用这种药物，

sentences.en: who may need to go on this medication.
sentences.zh: 或者可能需要服用这种药物。

sentences.en: Maybe you will have to one day and there's really no shame in that.
sentences.zh: 也许有一天你也必须服用，这真的没什么好羞耻的。

sentences.en: It's like taking a Panadol when you've got a headache.
sentences.zh: 这就好比头痛时吃一粒扑热息痛。

sentences.en: I think when we start seeing mental ill health as ill health that would be treated like we would treat a physical injury, a broken bone, a migraine,
sentences.zh: 我认为，当我们开始把心理健康问题视作一种健康问题——就像我们对待身体损伤、骨折、偏头痛一样来治疗，

sentences.en: you know, COVID, something like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，像新冠肺炎那样的情况。

sentences.en: And we're looking for treatment options and seeing those as part of that journey.
sentences.zh: 当我们寻找治疗方案并将它们视为这一历程的一部分时，

sentences.en: That's when we really start to actually respect mental ill health is just as valid as physical ill health.
sentences.zh: 我们才真正开始尊重心理健康问题，承认它与身体健康问题同样具有正当性。

sentences.en: Treatment and medication is a big part of that.
sentences.zh: 治疗和药物正是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to be kind of discussing today.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: And yeah, I hope that it's enjoyable when you gain something from this.
sentences.zh: 是的，希望这期节目会引人入胜，并且能让你们有所收获。

sentences.en: So perhaps the first thing we kind of need to wrap our heads around when we're talking about antidepressants is what exactly are they?
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们谈论抗抑郁药时，我们首先需要搞清楚的事情或许是：它们究竟是什么？

sentences.en: There is this great big myth, I think a lot of people pandered to, that they're kind of like a happy pill.
sentences.zh: 存在这样一个弥天大谎，我想很多人都在迎合它，即它们有点像是快乐药丸。

sentences.en: You know, you take your antidepressants and suddenly like the world's more colorful, everything feels better.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你吃了抗抑郁药，突然之间世界变得更绚丽了，一切都变好了。

sentences.en: And it's an easy way out for those who are experiencing depression or anxiety.
sentences.zh: 对于那些经历抑郁或焦虑的人来说，这是一种轻松的解脱方式。

sentences.en: That is absolutely not the case.
sentences.zh: 事实绝对并非如此。

sentences.en: At least it hasn't been my case in my experience with them.
sentences.zh: 至少在我使用它们的经历中并非如此。

sentences.en: Antidepressants work on the basis that there is a chemical imbalance in your brain that is causing you to experience happiness less frequently.
sentences.zh: 抗抑郁药起作用的基础是，你的大脑中存在化学失衡，导致你体验到快乐的频率降低。

sentences.en: It's causing you to experience more depressive episodes and depressive periods at a greater frequency and for a longer amount of time.
sentences.zh: 它导致你更频繁、更长时间地陷入抑郁发作期和抑郁阶段。

sentences.en: And with that, with many people who are experiencing that, it's also probably the case that you have higher levels of anxiety as well.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是，对于许多经历这种情况的人来说，你很可能也伴随着更高水平的焦虑。

sentences.en: Depression and anxiety, as we know, are often comorbid.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，抑郁症和焦虑症通常是共病的。

sentences.en: They happen hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 它们总是相伴发生。

sentences.en: And in kind of, you know, after the 70s, what doctors and psychologists began to realize is this isn't just, you know, because your life circumstances are crap
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你知道的，在20世纪70年代之后，医生和心理学家开始意识到，这不仅仅是因为你的人生处境糟糕透顶，

sentences.en: or because something traumatic has happened.
sentences.zh: 或者是因为发生了什么创伤性事件。

sentences.en: Depression is not just experience in moments of intense grief or intense suffering.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症不仅仅是在经历强烈的悲痛或强烈的痛苦时才会体验到。

sentences.en: It's something that people experience all the time, even when your life might be perfect, even when from the outside, everything seems to be going well.
sentences.zh: 它是人们无时无刻不在经历的事情，哪怕你的生活可能堪称完美，哪怕从外表来看一切都一帆风顺。

sentences.en: You've got food in your belly.
sentences.zh: 你丰衣足食。

sentences.en: You've got a family.
sentences.zh: 你有家庭。

sentences.en: You've got all the things that would fulfill you.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一切能够满足你心愿的事物。

sentences.en: There's something still quite not right.
sentences.zh: 但仍然有些地方不太对劲。

sentences.en: And what they identified that as being is a chemical imbalance in your brain, mostly and most often that being deficiency in dopamine or serotonin.
sentences.zh: 他们将其确定为大脑中的化学物质失衡，通常且最常见的情况是多巴胺或血清素的缺乏。

sentences.en: And it's not just that your brain isn't producing enough of these happy chemicals, as a lot of people call them, but it's that your brain is having difficulty
sentences.zh: 而且，这不仅在于你的大脑没有产生足够多这些被称为“快乐化学物质”的物质，还在于你的大脑在

sentences.en: transmitting them, processing them,
sentences.zh: 传递、处理它们，

sentences.en: and using them for the correct reasons.
sentences.zh: 以及为了正确目的而使用它们时遇到了困难。

sentences.en: So that's what the most common type of antidepressants, which are called selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, aim to kind of fix.
sentences.zh: 这就是最常见的抗抑郁药（被称为选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）旨在解决的问题。

sentences.en: So selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, we're going to call them SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 所以，选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂，我们简称它们为SSRIs。

sentences.en: You may have heard this term before, but they're the most common type of medication that someone experiencing depression or anxiety is most likely to be prescribed.
sentences.zh: 你可能以前听过这个词，但它们是经历抑郁或焦虑的人最有可能被开处方的最常见药物类型。

sentences.en: So how these work is,
sentences.zh: 那么这些药物是如何起作用的呢？

sentences.en: I guess we have to go back a step.
sentences.zh: 我想我们得倒退一步。

sentences.en: Our neurons communicate using chemical impulses, electrical impulses, but also chemical signals as well.
sentences.zh: 我们的神经元通过化学脉冲、电脉冲以及化学信号来进行交流。

sentences.en: So what these SSRIs are trying to do, they're not so much trying to address the electrical impulses, but the chemicals that these unlock.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些SSRIs试图做的事情，与其说它们试图处理电脉冲，不如说它们试图处理这些脉冲所释放的化学物质。

sentences.en: And these chemicals are things like serotonin, and dopamine.
sentences.zh: 这些化学物质就是血清素和多巴胺之类的东西。

sentences.en: So when those chemicals are released into the synapse, which is this little gap between your neurons, they send messages onto the next neuron
sentences.zh: 因此，当这些化学物质被释放到突触中（突触就是神经元之间的这个小间隙）时，它们会将信息发送到下一个神经元，

sentences.en: to elicit a certain feeling such as happiness or to create a behavioral action.
sentences.zh: 以引发某种感觉（例如快乐）或产生某种行为动作。

sentences.en: But if those chemicals are reabsorbed too quickly or they, you know, not enough of them is released, that's when we might start to experience
sentences.zh: 但如果这些化学物质被重新吸收得太快，或者它们（你知道的）释放量不足，这正是我们可能开始经历

sentences.en: in the long-term episodes of depression and of intense sadness.
sentences.zh: 长期抑郁发作和强烈悲伤的时候。

sentences.en: So what these drugs aim to do is they aim to block the sending neuron from taking back serotonin that it's released.
sentences.zh: 所以这些药物旨在做的是，它们旨在阻止发送神经元收回它已经释放的血清素。

sentences.en: So basically what that means is once a neuron releases serotonin, the happy hormone, the happy chemical, the SSRIs stop that neuron that sent it
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上意味着，一旦神经元释放了血清素（也就是快乐荷尔蒙、快乐化学物质），SSRIs就会阻止那个发送它的神经元

sentences.en: from kind of, you know, scooping it back up again.
sentences.zh: （你知道的）把它重新收回去。

sentences.en: So it means that more of that chemical becomes available within the synapse, essentially meaning that it changes the chemical structure of your brain
sentences.zh: 这意味着更多的这种化学物质能够在突触内保持可用状态，这本质上意味着它改变了你大脑的化学结构，

sentences.en: to be more receptive to serotonin, to have more serotonin and dopamine available to you, and therefore kind of change your life and change your kind of outlook on life.
sentences.zh: 让你对血清素更具接受度，使你有更多的血清素和多巴胺可资利用，从而改变你的生活以及你对人生的看法。

sentences.en: So what is your brain like on antidepressants if we have this kind of chemical understanding of how they work?
sentences.zh: 如果我们对它们的工作原理有了这种化学层面的理解，那么大脑在服用抗抑郁药时会是怎样的状态呢？

sentences.en: So like I said, there's this myth that they're happy pills, that they work kind of like ecstasy or some kind of like immediate, they provide this immediate jolt
sentences.zh: 所以就像我说的，存在这样一种神话，即它们是快乐药丸，它们的作用有点像摇头丸或某种即时起效的药物，它们能带来即时的冲击，

sentences.en: of just like pleasure and happiness and all your suffering ceases to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 带来纯粹的快乐和幸福，你所有的痛苦都不复存在。

sentences.en: And it's just not like that.
sentences.zh: 但事实根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: It's not a wave of joy.
sentences.zh: 它不是一股快乐的浪潮。

sentences.en: It's not a wave of ecstasy.
sentences.zh: 它不是一股摇头丸带来的狂喜浪潮。

sentences.en: What these hormones, what these, sorry, chemical kind of drugs intend to do is to push you back into equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 这些激素——抱歉，这些化学药物旨在做的是将你推回平衡状态。

sentences.en: They're not trying to like push you to the other side and make you deliriously happy.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是要把你推向另一个极端，让你欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: They want to kind of stabilize your brain so you're at a point where you can operate.
sentences.zh: 它们想要稳定你的大脑，让你处于一个能够正常运转的状态。

sentences.en: So basically, the way that I describe it is if you are someone who is depressed,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，我的描述方式是，如果你是一个抑郁的人——

sentences.en: like I have been for a big, you know, not a big part of my life, but for some of my life,
sentences.zh: 就像我在很大一部分时间里——也不是很大一部分时间，而在我生命中的某些时间里——经历过的那样，

sentences.en: what SSRIs do is they don't shift you all the way to this like other end of the scale.
sentences.zh: SSRIs的作用并不是把你一路推到量表的另一个极端。

sentences.en: They put you back in the middle.
sentences.zh: 它们把你拉回了中间。

sentences.en: And the result of that is that you no longer feel those like terrifying, awful black lows.
sentences.zh: 这样做的结果就是，你不再感受到那些可怕的、糟糕的黑色低谷。

sentences.en: But the other side of that is you no longer feel those highs as much.
sentences.zh: 但硬币的另一面是，你也同样不再那么强烈地感受到那些高峰。

sentences.en: You no longer feel that like, just like pure adrenaline of joy.
sentences.zh: 你不再感受到那种纯粹的快乐肾上腺素飙升。

sentences.en: The kind of upside being that you no longer have to experience those lows.
sentences.zh: 好的一面则是，你不再需要经历那些低谷。

sentences.en: It kind of steadies the roller coaster.
sentences.zh: 它有点像是在让过山车平稳下来。

sentences.en: If you can imagine like a roller coaster at Luna Park or like an amusement park, you know, the first part of the roller coaster is often like really up and down,
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象一下月神公园或游乐园里的过山车，你知道的，过山车的前半部分通常是起伏剧烈，

sentences.en: really up and down.
sentences.zh: 起伏非常剧烈。

sentences.en: You get those like the fear, the excitement, the anticipation.
sentences.zh: 你会体验到恐惧、兴奋、期待。

sentences.en: That's your brain without antidepressants.
sentences.zh: 这就是没有服用抗抑郁药的大脑。

sentences.en: It's just like chaotic and there's extreme lows and extreme highs.
sentences.zh: 它只是混乱不堪，有着极端的低谷和极端的高峰。

sentences.en: But on antidepressants, it's kind of like that end of the roller coaster.
sentences.zh: 但在服用了抗抑郁药之后，它有点像过山车的尾声。

sentences.en: There's still a few bumps, but they're not as significant.
sentences.zh: 仍然有一些颠簸，但没有那么剧烈了。

sentences.en: And it allows you to relax more.
sentences.zh: 它能让你更加放松。

sentences.en: You can see you're coming to the end of the ride.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到你正在接近行程的尾声。

sentences.en: That fear, that adrenaline kind of starts to decrease.
sentences.zh: 那种恐惧、那种肾上腺素开始逐渐消退。

sentences.en: And that's how antidepressants are intended to make you feel.
sentences.zh: 这就是抗抑郁药旨在让你感受到的状态。

sentences.en: So what does this kind of tell us about depression in general?
sentences.zh: 那么，这究竟向我们揭示了关于抑郁症的什么普遍规律呢？

sentences.en: So there's been so much research into SSRIs.
sentences.zh: 人们对SSRIs进行了大量的研究。

sentences.en: They were quite controversial when they first came out.
sentences.zh: 它们刚问世时曾引发相当大的争议。

sentences.en: They still are really misunderstood, but it tells us a kind of bigger story and paints a bigger picture around what the condition of depression actually is.
sentences.zh: 它们依然被严重误解，但它向我们讲述了一个更宏大的故事，描绘出抑郁症状况的真实全貌。

sentences.en: And that is, it's a chemical imbalance in your brain.
sentences.zh: 那就是，它是你大脑中的化学物质失衡。

sentences.en: Obviously, there are external factors that can make you depressed.
sentences.zh: 显然，有些外部因素会让你感到抑郁。

sentences.en: There are things that create deep suffering and deep grief.
sentences.zh: 有些事情会带来深重的痛苦和悲伤。

sentences.en: But everyday kind of run-of-the-mill depression, not that I really like to call it that, but the general disorder or the general illness that is depression is chemical,
sentences.zh: 但日常那种司空见惯的抑郁——虽然我不太喜欢这么叫它——不过作为一种普遍的失调或普遍的疾病，抑郁症是化学层面的，

sentences.en: it has a chemical origin in your brain.
sentences.zh: 它在大脑中有着化学根源。

sentences.en: And that's why SSRIs work so well because they stabilize that chemical imbalance.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂（SSRI）效果那么好，因为它们稳定了这种化学失衡。

sentences.en: They make more serotonin available to your brain and therefore contribute to kind of not so much a more positive outlook, but to a greater sense of control,
sentences.zh: 它们让你的大脑获得更多可用的5-羟色胺，因此与其说是带来更积极的视角，不如说是有助于增强掌控感，

sentences.en: a greater sense of kind of peace and happiness in your life.
sentences.zh: 增强你生活中的那种平静感和幸福感。

sentences.en: So my experience on antidepressants,
sentences.zh: 所以，我服用抗抑郁药的经历是这样的，

sentences.en: I don't really have a point of reference as to whether it's common, whether it is how everyone else experiences it.
sentences.zh: 我其实没有参考点来判断这是否常见，是否是其他所有人的体验。

sentences.en: But I would think that it is.
sentences.zh: 但我猜想是的。

sentences.en: Of the friends that I know who are also on this kind of medication that I'm on,
sentences.zh: 在我认识的也服用我这种药物的朋友中，

sentences.en: like they all kind of have said the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上都说过同样的话。

sentences.en: So for those who might not have the privilege of having friends who are going through similar things, I thought it would be maybe interesting to talk about what my experience
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些可能没有幸拥有经历过类似事情的朋友的人来说，我想聊聊我服用这种药物的经历可能会很有趣，

sentences.en: on this medication has been, why it has helped me, what it was like going on it, what it was like kind of going off for a while
sentences.zh: 它为什么帮助了我，刚开始吃是什么感觉，停药一段时间是什么感觉，

sentences.en: and what it's kind of done for my life.
sentences.zh: 以及它对我的生活产生了怎样的影响。

sentences.en: So I've been on antidepressants for two years.
sentences.zh: 所以，我服用抗抑郁药已经两年了。

sentences.en: I continue to be on them at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前我还在继续服用。

sentences.en: It is kind of normal for me to just take one once a day.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，每天吃一次已经成了一种常态。

sentences.en: And I find that especially when I first started taking them, it helped me a lot.
sentences.zh: 我发现，特别是在我刚开始吃的时候，它帮了我很多。

sentences.en: It really helped me at the point of my life that I was at.
sentences.zh: 在我当时经历的人生阶段，它确实帮了很大的忙。

sentences.en: I think if you met me as a person in real life and for those who do know me, I don't think that you would know that I've had experiences with depression in pretty dark times.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你在现实生活中遇到我，对于那些认识我的人来说，你大概不会知道我在相当黑暗的时期曾经历过抑郁。

sentences.en: I think I come off as very happy and pretty outgoing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我给人的印象非常快乐且外向。

sentences.en: Maybe you can hear that in the podcast and the things that I talk about are generally pretty upbeat or interesting.
sentences.zh: 也许你能在播客里听出来，我谈论的事情通常都相当轻松愉快或者很有趣。

sentences.en: They're not really about the sadness that has sometimes been in my life.
sentences.zh: 它们其实无关我生命中曾有过的悲伤。

sentences.en: But when I did decide to go on antidepressants, I went to my GP and I kind of explained everything that I'd been going through at that point.
sentences.zh: 但当我决定服用抗抑郁药时，我去找了全科医生，向他解释了我当时经历的一切。

sentences.en: I had mental health professionals around me, which were just an amazing asset.
sentences.zh: 我的身边有心理健康专业人士，他们真的是巨大的宝贵资源。

sentences.en: And he explained what this drug was, what this drug that he was going to prescribe me was, what he was going to prescribe me,
sentences.zh: 他向我解释了这种药是什么，他要给我开的是什么药，

sentences.en: what it was like and why he thought it would help me.
sentences.zh: 它是什么样的，以及他为什么认为它能帮到我。

sentences.en: And I remember him saying to me, this is not something you take for six months.
sentences.zh: 我记得他对我说过，这不是吃六个月的东西。

sentences.en: It's not something you take for a year.
sentences.zh: 这不是吃一年就能了事的。

sentences.en: It's something that you take for a while
sentences.zh: 这是你需要吃上一段时间的东西，

sentences.en: because your brain takes time to adjust and it's probably not particularly healthy to go off them cold turkey.
sentences.zh: 因为你的大脑需要时间适应，而且突然直接彻底停药可能并不是特别健康。

sentences.en: Now, this is really personal and I was kind of hesitant to talk about it, but I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 现在，这非常私密，我一开始有点犹豫要不要讲出来，但我觉得这很重要。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, what really drew me to take and to get on antidepressants was just the sense that what I was going through, I just couldn't endure it.
sentences.zh: 说到底，真正吸引我去服用抗抑郁药的原因，仅仅是我觉得我当时经历的一切，我实在无法忍受了。

sentences.en: I was really struggling and I don't think that's something that you need to be experiencing, especially with all the options these days.
sentences.zh: 我真的很挣扎，而且我认为没必要去经历那种痛苦，尤其是现在有这么多选择的情况下。

sentences.en: I'd been so hesitant about going on it before when it had been suggested to me.
sentences.zh: 以前当别人向我建议时，我对吃药一直非常犹豫。

sentences.en: I think because I myself was experiencing a lot of personal stigma around what it would mean for my character, the fact that I couldn't just persevere,
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我自己对它会意味着什么有着很多个人的耻辱感，觉得这有损我的人格，觉得自己无法单纯依靠毅力坚持下去，

sentences.en: the fact that I couldn't just change my life and make myself happy through daily habits and through exercise and healthy eating.
sentences.zh: 觉得自己无法仅仅通过日常习惯、运动和健康饮食来改变生活并让自己快乐。

sentences.en: But the thing that I came to realize is that taking medication is a daily habit.
sentences.zh: 但我后来意识到的是，服药本身就是一个日常习惯。

sentences.en: It is you taking action to help your brain, to help your body, to get better.
sentences.zh: 这是你在采取行动帮助你的大脑、帮助你的身体去变好。

sentences.en: So I went on them and the first experience that I really felt was just like extreme fatigue.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始吃药，我真正感受到的第一种体验就是极度疲惫。

sentences.en: So as my GP had explained, it takes a little bit of time to adjust to your new brain, I guess, to adjust to the fact that your brain suddenly has this new drug in its bloodstream,
sentences.zh: 正如我的全科医生所解释的那样，适应你的“新大脑”需要一点时间，我猜，就是去适应你的大脑血液中突然有了这种新药，

sentences.en: passing through the blood-brain barrier, creating chemical changes between your neurons.
sentences.zh: 它穿过血脑屏障，在你的神经元之间产生化学变化。

sentences.en: And I just felt so tired, so tired and numb for the first maybe month or two that I was on them.
sentences.zh: 在吃药的头一两个月里，我感觉自己太累了，疲惫又麻木。

sentences.en: And I was like, these are not working.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，这些药根本没用。

sentences.en: There is no point being on them.
sentences.zh: 吃它们毫无意义。

sentences.en: Yes, I don't feel sad, but I really don't feel anything at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不难过了，但我真的什么感觉也没有了。

sentences.en: Is that really how I want to feel?
sentences.zh: 这真的是我想过的感觉吗？

sentences.en: I think I particularly really like to feel elated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我特别喜欢那种欣喜若狂的感觉。

sentences.en: I like to feel extreme joy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢体验极致的快乐。

sentences.en: I like to experience hedonism and really enjoy my life.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢体验享乐主义并真正享受生活。

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, maybe it's worth
sentences.zh: 当时我想，好吧，也许为了获得欣喜、狂喜以及像对生活上瘾那样的回报，

sentences.en: experiencing those lows knowing that I get that reward of feeling elated and ecstatic and like high on life.
sentences.zh: 去经历那些低谷是值得的。

sentences.en: But like my GP said, it takes a couple of months, three months to kind of really see how your brain is going to react.
sentences.zh: 但就像我全科医生说的，需要几个月，三个月左右，才能真正看出你的大脑会有什么反应。

sentences.en: So I kept going and I kept putting, you know, kind of pushing through.
sentences.zh: 所以我坚持了下来，你知道的，咬牙坚持着。

sentences.en: And that fatigue went away.
sentences.zh: 那种疲惫感消失了。

sentences.en: Those, you know, sense, that sense of being heavy and of being numb went away.
sentences.zh: 那种沉重感和麻木感消失了。

sentences.en: The world became clearer and it also became more manageable.
sentences.zh: 世界变得更清晰了，也变得更可控了。

sentences.en: Before I went on them and before I went on my particular dosage, everything in my life just felt completely out of control.
sentences.zh: 在我吃药之前，在我服用特定剂量之前，我生活中的一切都感觉彻底失控。

sentences.en: Like I didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 就像我不知道该怎么办一样。

sentences.en: I couldn't force my brain to interpret situations the way that I wanted them to, I wanted it to.
sentences.zh: 我无法强迫我的大脑按照我想要的方式去诠释局势。

sentences.en: And like life was just like not feeling amazing.
sentences.zh: 生活感觉一点也不美妙。

sentences.en: And after three months, it may have been in combination with other lifestyle changes.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，这或许也是其他生活方式改变共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: Who can really say?
sentences.zh: 谁又能说得准呢？

sentences.en: Some people say it's placebo effect, but I did start to feel a lot better.
sentences.zh: 有些人说是安慰剂效应，但我确实开始感觉好多了。

sentences.en: I started to feel so many improvements in how I could identify my emotions and address them.
sentences.zh: 我开始感受到许多改善，表现在我如何识别自己的情绪并应对它们。

sentences.en: The one thing that did kind of stick around though is that experience that I've talked about a little bit earlier.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实有一点保留了下来，那就是我刚才稍微提过的那个体验。

sentences.en: Yes, I was not, you know, spending days in bed, but I also wasn't, you know, as excited by my life as I had been before.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不再（你知道的）整天躺在床上了，但我也（你知道的）不像以前那样对生活充满热情了。

sentences.en: Which was something that was really hard for me to give up.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是一件很难割舍的事。

sentences.en: But over time, it did start getting better.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，情况确实开始好转。

sentences.en: You know, as my brain adjusted to having this little helper and having this assistance,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，随着大脑适应了有这个小帮手和这种协助，

sentences.en: there started to be more of an equilibrium and a balance between those periods of like pure elation and joy and happiness.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的狂喜、快乐和幸福的时期之间，开始出现更多的平衡与协调。

sentences.en: And those lows weren't as deep, weren't as crushing, weren't as debilitating.
sentences.zh: 而那些低谷不再那么深渊般、不再那么粉碎人心、不再那么令人无力。

sentences.en: And I found that I could manage my life a lot more.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己能够更好地掌控生活了。

sentences.en: So that's the idea.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是当时的状况。

sentences.en: That's kind of what happened around starting.
sentences.zh: 这就是刚开始吃药时发生的事情。

sentences.en: Other things that I noticed was I was always thirsty.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的其他事情是，我总是口渴。

sentences.en: That was just like something really weird.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一件非常奇怪的事。

sentences.en: And I put on weight, which I didn't really mind because I was like, fuck it, that's totally worth it.
sentences.zh: 我还体重增加了，但我其实不在乎，因为我想管它的呢，绝对值得。

sentences.en: And I think that's about it.
sentences.zh: 我想大概就是这样吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had a bit of insomnia to begin with as well.
sentences.zh: 对，一开始我也经历了一点失眠。

sentences.en: But I think that was just the fact that I was also really anxious.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得那只是因为我当时也真的很焦虑。

sentences.en: But all in all, after three months, it all just kind of started to kind of figure itself out.
sentences.zh: 不过总的来说，三个月后，一切都开始自己理顺了。

sentences.en: And since then,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，

sentences.en: I've kind of been on them and there was a point when I decided that, you know, I wanted to stop.
sentences.zh: 我一直都在吃药，直到有一天我决定，你知道的，我想停药了。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be on these for much longer.
sentences.zh: 我不想再继续吃这些药了。

sentences.en: Kind of thought about how long I'd been taking this medication, read a few books that I probably shouldn't have read about like alternative therapies.
sentences.zh: 当时琢磨着自己吃这药有多久了，还读了几本关于另类疗法的书，其实我本不该读的。

sentences.en: You know, do your research, I guess, if that's the thing you want to read.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看那种书，去做好调查研究吧。

sentences.en: And if you want to think about other ways to manage depression or anxiety, if you're experiencing it, it's totally up to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你想寻找其他方法来应对抑郁或焦虑，如果你正在经历这些，那完全取决于你。

sentences.en: But always seek healthcare advice, I think, is the thing.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得最重要的是，永远要寻求医疗建议。

sentences.en: And there are some like pretty serious dangers if you decide to stop taking your antidepressant, your SSRI, like cold turkey.
sentences.zh: 如果你决定突然彻底停掉抗抑郁药、你的SSRI，会有一些相当严重的危险。

sentences.en: It's like withdrawal from any other type of drug.
sentences.zh: 这就像戒掉任何其他类型的毒品一样。

sentences.en: Your brain is addicted to it.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑对它上瘾了。

sentences.en: You are taking it regularly.
sentences.zh: 你在规律地服用它。

sentences.en: Your brain is not used to operating without it.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑已经习惯不了没有它的运作方式。

sentences.en: And I won't lie, I think about stopping every month.
sentences.zh: 我不撒谎，我每个月都想过停药。

sentences.en: There will be days when I just don't take my antidepressant or sometimes even, you know, half a week.
sentences.zh: 总会有那么几天我就是不吃抗抑郁药，有时甚至（你知道的）断药半周。

sentences.en: I think the most was a week.
sentences.zh: 我想最长的一次是一周。

sentences.en: And at that point, after a week of not taking it, oh my God, did I start to notice.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，断药一周后，天哪，我可开始有感觉了。
